scope: New LLVM temporary archive predicate and Windows filesystem regression; no local or native execution
conclusion: No blocking defect found in the narrowly reviewed predicate and test. The original Windows/Linux process-wrapper suites and failing original Clippy path still require exact-head execution.
confirmed: New exclusion requires an archive prefix ending .lib, .rlib or .a, the .temp-archive- separator, exactly seven ASCII hexadecimal digits, and final .a after ASCII case folding.
Filename filtering does not add any broad NotFound, permission or copy-error swallowing. Existing hard-link fallback to copy and its error propagation remain unchanged.
Existing .tmp and .rcgu.o exclusions are preserved rather than broadened by the new archive test.

Regression creates ten final or nearby names and five temporary outputs on the real filesystem, invokes consolidate_dependency_search_paths, compares every retained payload byte, checks every excluded name absent and checks the final directory count.

Test uses a path with spaces, a Unicode filename and mixed-case hex; final .lib/.rlib/.a, wrong suffix, six/eight digits, nonhex, extra suffix and missing archive-prefix cases remain in the expected output set.
Module is Windows-test-only; upstream imports, guard constructor and ProcessWrapperError Error implementation support the new fixture's use.
limits: The filesystem regression is a deterministic name-selection check, not a concurrent LLVM rename stress test.
A deliberately named final file matching the exact reserved temporary shape is indistinguishable by filename alone; this change relies on the compiler temporary-name convention.
No test counts or production qualification are claimed by this static review.
